notes: No supplied study, description, outcome, sample or test locator selects an original result. No selection by row order, replication author or numeric matching. The source is verified as Bateson (2012). Table 4 p. 575 (PDF p. 6, rendered and visually inspected) contains multiple OLS crime-victimization coefficients: candidate Latin America/Caribbean community action 0.0334 with p<0.001; candidate US/Canada community action 0.0695 with p<0.001; candidate Europe political conversations 0.0189 with p<0.01. Bounds follow stars on the same respective coefficients and the printed legend; these are separate candidate tests, not assigned values. Table 4 rescales dependent variables to endpoints 0 and 1; coefficients are not identified as standardized. No effect conversion. Further candidates include probit/ordered-probit first differences (pp. 575–577), crime-type regressions (pp. 577–578), controls/matching/placebo tests (pp. 579–581), and political attitudes (p. 583). The p. 572 typical country respondent range is not critical-model analytic N. Table 4 prints coefficients/robust SEs, without model observation counts. Table notes exclude Lesotho because district was not recorded and Indonesia because Urban was not recorded. Respondents are participants; clustering varies by survey across municipality, state/province, district, region and country. No common model N established; no final mutually exclusive groups summed; no arithmetic or df-based N derivation.
